newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar recovers to close stronger.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar recovers to close stronger.

text.p: The Canadian dollar staged a strong recovery in afternoon trading Friday to close at C$1.3699 (US$0.7300) from Thursday's close of C$1.3755 (US$0.7270).
When the currency failed to break through a key technical point at C$1.3785, a diverse range of buyers were encouraged to come back into the market, dealers said.
Trading was heavy as market players decided the Canadian currency was undervalued, they said.
"It's typical of the way the Canadian dollar is traded," said one dealer.
Investors were also encouraged by an improving mood in the Canadian stock and bond markets, dealers said.
The bond, stock and currency markets were all hit hard in Canada on Thursday. The Canadian dollar closed at its weakest point since August.
But traders cautioned that Friday's strength may be shortlived, partly because of fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve may raise interest rates.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar firmed to 1.1422 marks from the 1.1206 mark close on Thursday and rebounded to 84.88 yen from 84.04 yen.
